newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australia backs Calliope nickel plan.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australia backs Calliope nickel plan.

text.p: The Australian government on Monday backed a proposal by a subsidiary of Calliope Metals Corp to build a nickel/cobalt processing plant in Queensland.

Federal Industry Minister John Moore and Queensland Industry Minister Bruce Davidson said in a statement Canberra had given the project major project facilitation status, enabling the proposal to be approved quickly with state and federal co-ordination.
"The aim of the government is to create the right investment environment for this to occur," Moore said in a statement.

Calliope Metals Pty Ltd plans to build a two-stage nickel/cobalt processing plant near Gladstone in Queensland with an initial capital expenditure of A$225 million, rising to A$350 million if the refinery is developed, Moore and Davidson said.
Stage one of the project was expected to generate a net export income of about A$260 million per annum, they said.
"Stage one involves the importation of nickel/cobalt ore from New Caledonia for processing into a mixed sulphide intermediate product for export," they said.
"Stage two involves the development of a refinery to further process the product into nickel and cobalt metal."
Construction could start in January 1998 with the first marketable sulphides produced in early 1999.

Moore said minerals processing was an industry with big opportunities. "Smelting and refining all of Australia's minerals production for example, would increase exports by A$30-A$50 billion per annum, and make a significant contribution to reducing our current account deficit," Moore said.
Calliope Metals Pty Ltd is wholly owned by Calliope Metals Corp, which has raised A$4.5 million in development capital for the Queensland project.
